Anchor a bare card in the user's timezone. 0.6.2 removed push's dependency on the agent re-piping sessions but left the same dependency on tz: with TZ unset in the container a bare card resolved to UTC and stored the UTC wall-clock as local, moving an evening session to the next day. fetch now remembers the server-supplied tz and push falls back to it.

- Internal version updated to 0.6.1.

Every card gets a day. fetch now remembers each returned session's raw start/end instants in per-user state (30-day TTL, 500-entry cap), and push resolves the card's journal window from the union of that memory and any piped sessions. A bare card object piped to push now still gets its capture day instead of pinning to today forever. No date is ever invented: when both sources miss, the card is written undated as before.

javis-brainstorming 0.5.0

- Changed dispatcher behavior: The javis-server now invokes this skill directly on every completed unit (no classifier or route matching), relying on the skill agent to determine if action is needed.
- Clarified agent discretion: The skill will only produce a to-do card if its own agent identifies a brainstorm-worthy request; otherwise, it remains silent.
- Minor documentation adjustments: Updated SKILL.md to explain the new invocation flow and agent responsibility.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.

- Removed the skill-card.md file to simplify documentation.
- No changes to code or core functionality.

- Cards are now stamped with the source session's start/end times (journal semantics), improving calendar integration and event tracking.
- On iOS, Confirm now saves the to-do card as a solid calendar event at the session time; tapping opens its Agent Chat session instead of just copying the prompt.
- When pushing a card, the sessions and timezone must be included so the script can extract and assign accurate journal times to the card.
- The previous sample file skill-card.md was removed.
- Updated documentation to clarify workflow, payload structure, calendar behavior, and date handling.

- Removed the redundant skill-card.md file for a slimmer package.
- The skill now delivers a markdown digest of each to-do card to Agent Chat via POST /api/agent/push, so summaries appear in the chat ([push:javis-brainstorming] + card summary).
- Updated push step: after writing a pending to-do card, it also delivers a chat digest (chat delivery is non-fatal and reports success/failure).
- Clarified description and workflow to reflect that chat digests are now sent on every card push.

Version 0.1.1 of javis-brainstorming

- Skill name updated from "brainstorming" to "javis-brainstorming" for consistency.
- Route configuration and metadata updated to reference the new skill name.
- No logic or behavior changes were introduced in this release.

- Initial release of the "brainstorming" skill for generating ready-to-paste to-do cards, enabling seamless hand-off to Claude’s content-brainstorming workflow.
- Automatically or on-demand detects brainstorm-worthy requests in transcripts, then composes and saves a “todo” card without doing any brainstorming itself.
- Card is presented in the iOS Calendar tab, with "Confirm" copying a pre-filled Claude prompt to the clipboard.
- Fetches up to 24 hours of transcript data by default; deduplicates cards on push.
- Supports triggers such as "brainstorm this", "整理成簡報", and "帮我腦力激盪", with full support for auto-run via the session dispatcher.
